hints.title: Use equal distances to the centres
hints.body: At either common point, the distances to the two centres are equal because the circles have the same radius. Call that common radius r.
hints.recap: Points equally distant from two fixed centres lie on their perpendicular bisector.
hints.pitfall: The desired line is perpendicular to the line of centres, not the line joining those centres.
hints.pause: Write the two circle equations with the same <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: Points equally distant from two fixed centres lie on their perpendicular bisector.

hints.title: Subtract to remove the radius
hints.body: The equations are (x+2)2+(y−1)2=r2 and (x−3)2+(y+2)2=r2. Subtract one equation from the other.
hints.recap: Subtracting equal-distance equations cancels the squared coordinates and the common radius.
hints.pitfall: Subtract every term of the second expression, including its constant terms.
hints.pause: Expand the differences and simplify to a linear equation.

recall.reminder: Subtracting equal-distance equations cancels the squared coordinates and the common radius.

hints.title: Match the equation without solving the points
hints.body: After subtraction, the squared coordinates and common radius cancel. Collect the remaining x terms, y terms and constants. Both given intersection points satisfy this resulting linear relation.
hints.recap: A common linear relation can identify the joining line without finding either intersection point.
hints.pitfall: The unknown numerical radius is not needed.
hints.pause: Simplify the linear relation and rearrange it into one of the offered forms.

recall.reminder: A common linear relation can identify the joining line without finding either intersection point.

solution:
The two circle equations are (x+2)2+(y−1)2=r2 and (x−3)2+(y+2)2=r2. Subtracting the second from the first cancels x2, y2 and r2, leaving 10x−6y−8=0.

Therefore both common points lie on 5x−3y=4, the perpendicular bisector of the centres. This is F.
